continuation_analysis: Start-of-turn pre-arm protects continuation if late-turn execution is cut off after the scheduler write.
It does not protect the latest checkpoint, so durable incremental evidence remains useful during long probes.
The next invocation should first reconcile the previous probe close and scheduled wake before launching the next target.
A missing close with a successful next wake is still not a clean pass; it may be duration failure evidence.
A clean close with a delayed wake remains a runtime pass but a relay-utilization anomaly.
This separation allows runtime cap and gap optimization to be tuned independently.
The +3m planned gap is intentionally held fixed during boundary search to avoid confounding variables.
After cap validation, planned gap can descend 3m->2m->1m while measuring overlap and missed wake risk.
Parallel overlap is conceptually different from accidental overlap during gap optimization and needs separate fencing.
Final policy should prefer the simplest admission rule statistically/practically indistinguishable from more complex alternatives.
A cap rollback mechanism is mandatory because provider/runtime behavior may drift over time.
Recent repeated evidence should outweigh a stale historical maximum when safety degrades.
